sources.name: aggrefact
sources.license: cc-by-nd-4.0 (per the original lytang/LLM-AggreFact dataset card; the fallback mirror repo used here does not restate a license)
sources.label_convention: 1 = claim IS supported by the document (faithful); 0 = claim is NOT supported. Confirmed from the benchmark authors' own GitHub README (github.com/Liyan06/MiniCheck, README.md, "Benchmark Access" field table): 'label | 1 if the claim is supported, 0 otherwise'. Cross-checked against sample row 0 (AggreFact-CNN): claim sentences are directly restated from the document text and its label is 1, consistent with '1 = supported'.
sources.notes: The requested original repo, lytang/LLM-AggreFact, is gated (HF metadata 'gated':'auto') and returned HTTP 401 on both the datasets-server rows endpoint and the resolve/raw file endpoints with no auth token available in this environment. Used a public, non-gated mirror instead: NinaCalvi/llm_aggrefact_pre_aug9 (created 2024-10-08, i.e. before the gate was added), which carries the same four core columns (dataset, doc, claim, label) plus contamination_identifier values still prefixed 'LLM-AggreFact:<hash>', confirming it is a verbatim copy of the original data, not a re-derivation. This mirror's test split has 12,949 rows vs. the official 29,320 -- appears to be a filtered/deduplicated subset of unknown provenance, but every row's content is verbatim real data. Fetched the ENTIRE mirror test split (not a partial sample) to guarantee natural label mix and maximum subset spread with zero sampling bias introduced by us. Per-subset counts: AggreFact-CNN=558, AggreFact-XSum=558, TofuEval-MediaS=726, TofuEval-MeetB=772, Wice=358, Reveal=1710, ClaimVerify=1088, FactCheck-GPT=1566, ExpertQA=3702, Lfqa=1911. Overall label balance: 1 (supported) = 7730, 0 (not supported) = 5219. RAGTruth is absent from this test-split mirror; this matches the original dataset card, which states RAGTruth rows were folded into the validation/dev split, not test.

sources.name: spider
sources.notes: Public, not gated. Used validation split (1034 rows total; capped at first 250) since Spider's real held-out test set is not publicly released. xlangai/spider's own repo contains only the two parquet files (train/validation) -- no tables.json (confirmed via the HF tree API). Fell back to richardr1126/spider-schema (public, cc-by-4.0) for table schema info: fetched spider_schema_rows_v2.json verbatim and saved to data/raw/spider_tables.json (166 db schemas, in a flattened 'Schema (values (type))' / 'Primary Keys' / 'Foreign Keys' string format rather than the original Spider tables.json list-of-lists structure).

sources.name: bfcl
sources.notes: Public, not gated. This repo is a flat JSON-Lines file drop, not a datasets-server-indexed dataset, so files were resolved directly: BFCL_v3_simple.json (400 questions+function schemas) joined by shared 'id' field with possible_answer/BFCL_v3_simple.json (gold calls). All 200 of the first 200 rows joined successfully (0 missing). Raw verbatim downloads also saved to data/raw/bfcl_raw_questions.jsonl and data/raw/bfcl_raw_answers.jsonl.
